title: Seniors Aged 55 and Above Who Benefited from Senior Worker Support Package
what_it_is: Seniors Aged 55 and Above Who Benefited from Senior Worker Support Package

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Following 2019 Tripartite Workgroup recommendations, the retirement age and re-employment age will rise to 63 and 68 from 1 July 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In line with the 2019 recommendations by the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, the retirement age and re-employment age will be increased to 63 and 68 respectively, and this will take effect from 1 July 2022.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit disbursements
sections.summary: The Senior Employment Credit, started 1 January 2021, has disbursed close to $150 million to 86,000 employers, benefiting 482,000 senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Senior Employment Credit started from 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Thus far, close to $150 million have been disbursed to 86,000 employers, benefiting 482,000 senior workers.

sections.label: Senior employment rates during pandemic
sections.summary: Despite COVID-19, the employment rate of those aged 55 to 64 held steady above 67%, while the rate for those 65 and above rose from 27.6% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, the employment rate of those aged 55 to 64 held steady at over 67%, while the employment rate of those aged 65 and above has increased from 27.6% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2020.

sections.label: Senior Worker Support Package funding
sections.summary: Senior worker employment rates have held up, and the Government allocated S$1.5 billion through the Senior Worker Support Package over three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Senior worker employment rates have held up and the Government has allocated S$1.5 billion through the Senior Worker Support Package over three years.

sections.label: Raising ages and JGI uptake
sections.summary: The passage states a path to raise the retirement age eventually to 65 and re-employment age to 70, and asks how many companies took up JGI.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, we have a very clear sustained path to raise the retirement age, eventually to 65, and the re-employment age to 70.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think that will be the first phase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are also talking to other OECD countries where we are looking at beyond a certain age, work, and retirement ages and re-employment ages could be adjusted according to the healthy life expectancy of the population at that point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Despite all this, many aged 40 and above still struggle to seek re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister how many companies have taken up JGI and taken full use of this incentive?
